title: Boring, Sideways Day. Does Wednesday's Fed Announcement Even Matter?
summary:
Boring, Sideways Day. Does Wednesday's Fed Announcement Even Matter? 

             
             
            Neocloud concerns continued to experience a small correction/consolidation after last week's surge. Interest rates could have justified a bit of weakness as a result, but managed to hold fairly steady. Bond market indecision likely has more to do with that and less to do with any sort of Fed Day anticipation. Markets have almost fully priced in a "pause." Any Fed-induced volatility would thus be dependent on verbiage--either in the announcement itself or the 2:30pm ET press conference. This is one of those Fed meetings that could be entirely forgettable, but post-press-conference volatility should never be ruled out as a risk--even on seemingly low consequence Fed days.

title: Mortgage Rates Hold Steady Yet Again
summary: It was a remarkably calm day for the mortgage market on two separate levels. First off, the average lender set this morning's rates right in line with yesterday's latest levels. Additionally, there were very few intraday changes (and in those cases, rates improved modestly).  [thirtyyearmortgagerates]  All of the above is made possible by the fact that the bond market stayed right in line with yesterday's levels all day long. This has happened for two straight days now, and it's the sort of stability that seemed like a distant memory several weeks ago.  Will it last?  There's never any way to know for sure. The bond/rate market is constantly at risk of responding to several sources of motivation. It just so happens that those sources have been silent after last week's improvement.   It's worth noting that there's a new Fed rate announcement tomorrow. Fed announcements often create volatility for rates and that volatility is rarely related to whether the Fed hikes/cuts/holds steady. In tomorrow's case, we already have a high degree of certainty that the Fed will not be hiking rates. Any impact the Fed has on mortgage rates would be a factor of the words they use in the policy statement or the words spoken by Fed Chair Warsh in the 2:30pm ET press conference.   Beyond the Fed, there are still other potential considerations for rates (tech sector volatility, war-related headlines), but never any guarantee that they'll adhere to a certain timeline.

title: Appraisal Review, Equity, QC Tools; Jumbo Competition, Microsoft News Implications? STRATMOR Tech Survey
summary: The ancient Chinese philosopher Sun Tzu said, “Sometimes the best victory is the battle that was not fought.” In a shrinking residential market there are a lot of potential battles, for example: “Rob, are you hearing that some IMBs are not charging an origination fee or putting caps on LO comp for jumbo loans?” Of course, especially if the independent mortgage bank, or broker, is in an area where’s you’re battling it out with credit unions and banks. If you have a $2 million loan, and an IMB’s LO is charging a point, that’s $20k, but if an originator at a CU or depository bank is charging $5,000 for the same loan because they’re capped at that, well, what’s borrower supposed to do? So, yes, many IMBs do cap comp or origination fees. Not only that, but with interest rates where they are, and jumbo adjustable rate mortgages a viable product, often banks and CUs have a solid offering. There are some good deals to be had because of the poor affordability, but buyers not in the business of buying homes have a hard time wrapping their head around all of it versus five years ago. title: Mostly Consolidating Ahead of Fed. Some Pressure From Neocloud Bounce
summary: "Neocloud" has entered the commentary. This is shorthand for the market segment in which Coreweave operates. Neocloud companies have been the epicenter of recent concerns in tech that have helped fuel the mid October bond rally.  Their negative momentum leveled off last Thursday--the same time bond yields bottomed. Neocloud stocks are up sharply this morning and their bond yields are falling. Coreweave yields are back to last Wednesday's levels (though still hugely elevated from early October levels). The consolidation mirrors the bond market over the past several sessions, although this morning's Durable Goods data made for a slight bump in yields. Wednesday's Fed announcement is likely the next major scheduled event that could serve as the jumping-off point for the next phase of momentum.

title: Young Homebuying Falls 15%, But Purchases With Older Co-Borrowers Hold Steady
summary: Young Americans are buying fewer homes than they were seven years ago, but purchases involving older co-applicants are bucking the trend.Home purchases by borrowers under 35 have fallen 15% since 2018, while purchases involving a co-applicant age 55 or older have increased roughly 3%, according to a new Rocket Mortgage analysis of Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) data released Tuesday.

title: Friday Harbor Expands AI Appraisal Reviews As UAD 3.6 Deadline Nears
summary: With the November 2 deadline for new appraisal reporting requirements approaching, lenders face a choice: complete their transition to Uniform Appraisal Dataset (UAD) 3.6 or seek additional time under a temporary exception that carries consequences next year.The approaching mandate is also driving technology changes across the mortgage industry. On Tuesday, Friday Harbor announced that it has expanded its AI-powered appraisal review platform to support UAD 3.6 reports, with more than 350 automated checks designed to identify potential issues and reduce manual review work.
